email.body1:
Jamie, saw Qualia added Customers Bank and Axos to the Bank Partner Network in early 2026.

Expanding enterprise relationships that fast usually means more named accounts in play than the team can cover before deals cool, and that gap is where enterprise pipeline slips. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Qualia off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jamie, quick follow-up for Qualia.

As the bank network grows, the enterprise target list expands faster than headcount can. Most leaders don't actually know how many meetings each rep needs to cover the new accounts, so the gap surfaces late in the quarter when it is hardest to recover.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Qualia needs to keep enterprise coverage intact without hiring a wave of reps.
email.body3:
Jamie, last bit of proof for Qualia.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Qualia's reply rate likely compares to other enterprise software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jamie, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Onboarding new bank partners is its own kind of busy, and timing matters most here.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise motion? I'll tailor it to Qualia either way.
